prompt: CHALLENGE: A spectrum shows M⁺ at m/z 86 (intensity 100%) and M+1 at m/z 87 (intensity 5.5%). Using the fact that each ¹³C contributes ~1.1% to M+1, estimate the number of carbons AND propose a formula.

options.label: ~5 carbons (5 × 1.1 = 5.5). With M = 86 and 5 C (60 mass units), the remaining 26 fits C₅H₁₀O (hexanal / 2-hexanone / pentanal etc.) or C₅H₁₀N... actually C₅H₁₀O = 86 ✓
The compound must contain nitrogen (odd mass rule)

explanation: Dividing observed M+1 intensity (5.5%) by per-C contribution (~1.1%) gives # of C atoms. 5.5 / 1.1 = 5. M = 86 − (5×12) = 26 mass units remaining. 26 = 10 H + 1 O → C₅H₁₀O. Rings/degrees-of-unsaturation = 1 (DoU) → an aldehyde or ketone fits (e.g., 2-pentanone has M = 86).
